-- 166_identity_need_icf_owner_review.sql
-- SCHEMA migration -- compensating migration for 165 (T-145), made after the adversarial pass on it. 165 is committed,
-- so it is not edited (rule 3); the table it made is EMPTY on every database (no triple has been written: derive
-- `select count(*) from identity_need_icf`), so it is dropped and recreated rather than altered. Tooling, no rows.
--
-- WHAT THE PASS FOUND, and what this changes:
--  1. "Only the owner's review makes a row stated" was held by nothing: `reviewed_by` was free text, and the session
--     that ran the review was recorded nowhere. A review is now BOUND to the owner's words, as retire-identity and
--     add-jurisdiction already bind theirs: `review_ref` is the heading of a dated ledger entry that begins "Owner" and
--     names the triple as the token TRIPLE-<id>. `reviewed_by` is gone (the entry says who); `reviewed_session` records
--     the session that ran the verb.
--  2. A reject discarded who authorised it. `retirement_ref` holds the owner entry that rejected the row.
--  3. "Never revived" was a sentence. The trigger below makes the schema refuse an edit of a retired row, of a row's
--     three keys, warrant or origin, and of a review once recorded (a data migration rendered by emit_batch_sql can
--     carry an UPDATE).
--  4. Unchanged, and now read: `review_note` and the retirement cells appear on `lens-crosswalk` (the view carries the
--     caveat and the owner entry; `--retired` lists the rejected rows with their reasons).
--
-- WRITERS: db.py propose-identity-need-icf, review-identity-need-icf. READERS: v_lens_crosswalk, read by db.py
-- lens-crosswalk (--retired reads the table). No AFTER_DATA marker: the table is new to every data migration.

DROP VIEW IF EXISTS v_lens_crosswalk;
DROP TABLE identity_need_icf;

CREATE TABLE identity_need_icf (
    triple_id           INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    identity_code       TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES base_taxonomy_identity(identity_code),
    need_code           TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES access_needs(need_code),
    icf_code            TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES base_icf(icf_code),
    state               TEXT NOT NULL
                        CHECK (state IN ('stated', 'provisional', 'pending', 'not_applicable')),
    warrant             TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(trim(warrant)) > 0),
    created_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_by_session  TEXT NOT NULL,
    -- THE OWNER'S REVIEW: the heading of the ledger entry that records it, the time, and the session that ran the verb.
    review_ref          TEXT CHECK (review_ref IS NULL OR review_ref LIKE 'Owner%'),
    reviewed_at         TEXT,
    reviewed_session    TEXT,
    review_note         TEXT CHECK (review_note IS NULL OR length(trim(review_note)) > 0),
    retired_at          TEXT,
    retired_by_session  TEXT,
    retirement_reason   TEXT,
    retirement_ref      TEXT CHECK (retirement_ref IS NULL OR retirement_ref LIKE 'Owner%'),
    CHECK ((review_ref IS NULL) = (reviewed_at IS NULL) AND (review_ref IS NULL) = (reviewed_session IS NULL)),
    CHECK (state NOT IN ('stated', 'provisional') OR reviewed_at IS NOT NULL),
    CHECK (state <> 'pending' OR reviewed_at IS NULL),
    CHECK ((state = 'provisional') = (review_note IS NOT NULL)),
    CHECK ((retired_at IS NULL AND retired_by_session IS NULL AND retirement_reason IS NULL AND retirement_ref IS NULL)
        OR (retired_at IS NOT NULL AND retired_by_session IS NOT NULL AND length(trim(retirement_reason)) > 0
            AND retirement_ref IS NOT NULL))
);

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ux_identity_need_icf_live
    ON identity_need_icf (identity_code, need_code, icf_code)
 WHERE retired_at IS NULL;

CREATE TRIGGER identity_need_icf_no_edit BEFORE UPDATE ON identity_need_icf
WHEN OLD.retired_at IS NOT NULL
  OR NEW.identity_code IS NOT OLD.identity_code OR NEW.need_code IS NOT OLD.need_code
  OR NEW.icf_code IS NOT OLD.icf_code OR NEW.warrant IS NOT OLD.warrant
  OR NEW.created_at IS NOT OLD.created_at OR NEW.created_by_session IS NOT OLD.created_by_session
  OR (OLD.reviewed_at IS NOT NULL AND (NEW.state IS NOT OLD.state OR NEW.review_ref IS NOT OLD.review_ref
      OR NEW.reviewed_at IS NOT OLD.reviewed_at OR NEW.reviewed_session IS NOT OLD.reviewed_session
      OR NEW.review_note IS NOT OLD.review_note))
BEGIN
    SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'identity_need_icf: a retired row, a triple''s keys and warrant, and a recorded review are never edited; retire the row and propose a new one');
END;

CREATE VIEW v_lens_crosswalk AS
SELECT t.triple_id, t.identity_code, i.display_name AS identity_name,
       t.need_code, n.design_obligation AS need_obligation,
       t.icf_code, c.title AS icf_title,
       t.state, t.warrant, t.review_note, t.review_ref, t.reviewed_at, t.created_by_session
  FROM identity_need_icf t
  JOIN base_taxonomy_identity i ON i.identity_code = t.identity_code
  JOIN access_needs n           ON n.need_code     = t.need_code
  JOIN base_icf c               ON c.icf_code      = t.icf_code
 WHERE t.retired_at IS NULL;

PRAGMA user_version = 166;
-- 165_identity_need_icf.sql
-- SCHEMA migration -- the judged identity, access-need and ICF matrix (T-145). Tooling, no research rows: the triples
-- that fill it are a later research pull request the owner reviews.
--
-- WHY. Owner, 2026-11-20: readers will navigate the repository first by a disability identity, and "you basically need
-- to have a big 3D matrix of ICF codes * access needs * disability identities" ("yes, correct" to a table of judged
-- triples). Today an identity cannot say which access needs it has, and 11 of the 23 identities name no ICF code
-- (derive: task T-145 section 3). access_needs.absorbs holds identities as a delimited cell, which one value per cell
-- (2026-11-06) does not allow to stay the only home. Ledger: `grep -n -F "Owner statements 2026-11-20 (fifth)"
-- references/project-standards.md`.
--
-- ALL THREE KEYS, EACH NOT NULL (owner, 2026-11-20: "should be all three"). A cell of the cube has three coordinates.
-- What is known of only two is a `gaps` row (gaps carries identity_code, icf_code and needs_code), not a stored row.
-- D-0182 (at least one lens) governs a determination and is not touched.
--
-- STORED SPARSELY. A cell with no row reads as not yet judged. A `not_applicable` row reads as judged and not
-- applying. Both carry the same warrant (a quiet "does not apply" is the failure the cell states exist to prevent).
--
-- THE STATES. A session proposes a triple as `pending` (judged to apply) or `not_applicable` (judged not to). Only the
-- review verb, run on the owner's review of a batch, sets `stated` (or `provisional`, accepted with a caveat held in
-- review_note); the CHECKs below refuse a stated or provisional row with no reviewer, and a pending row with one.
-- A row the owner rejects is retired in place with the reason; a retired row is never revived (write a new one).
--
-- NOT CHANGED. identity_icf_map (61 rows), access_need_icf (43) and access_needs.absorbs stay as the maps a session
-- reads when it proposes (T-126). They propose; this table judges. `absorbs` is retired by a later schema migration
-- once triples cover every need, placed after every data migration that INSERTs it (rule 5).
--
-- No AFTER_DATA marker: the table is new, so no committed data migration can INSERT into it.
--
-- WRITERS: db.py propose-identity-need-icf, review-identity-need-icf. READERS: the view v_lens_crosswalk, read by
-- db.py lens-crosswalk (from an identity, a need or an ICF code; --uncovered lists identities and needs with no live
-- triple, which are the gaps ACTION 3 of the ledger entry says to close). All three keys are base tables, so the view
-- crosses no stage (CLAUDE.md section 3).

CREATE TABLE identity_need_icf (
    triple_id           INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    identity_code       TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES base_taxonomy_identity(identity_code),
    need_code           TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES access_needs(need_code),
    icf_code            TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES base_icf(icf_code),
    state               TEXT NOT NULL

5724:## Convention 2026-11-12 — how a delegated resolution's standing is recorded, and when it opens a task's gate
5903:Recorded in the same pass, as an addendum to "Convention 2026-11-12 — how a delegated resolution's standing is recorded, and when it opens a task's gate" (entry above). **A convention for reading the ledger, not an owner ruling**; the owner may replace it. The Definition of Done (`workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/REMEDIATION-WORKPLAN.md` §10, D-27) has always allowed a decision to end as "deferred by the owner", but the convention gave that no status value, so no command could find it.
5734:**The gate.** A task's precondition on a decision is OPEN only when (1) the last status line is `ANSWERED BY THE OWNER`, or (2) the last status line is `RESOLVED UNDER DELEGATION` **and** the last check line is `not required`, `confirmed` or `confirmed with corrections applied`. Every other state is CLOSED, including no status line at all, `pending`, a withdrawn resolution and a referral. **A task whose text requires the owner's own words** (for example the mobility split, T-102) **is open only on `ANSWERED BY THE OWNER`**; a delegated resolution never satisfies it. The one command a task file uses:

39:## 4. The change, and the four questions that are the owner's
40-
41-A table of judged links, stored sparsely: a cell with no row reads as not yet judged; a row in the not-applicable state reads as judged and not applying. Following the shape of `identity_icf_map` (the nearest sibling): its own primary key, real foreign keys to `base_taxonomy_identity`, `access_needs` and `base_icf`, a warrant held in the table's own cells (never a pointer to a ledger heading), `created_by_session`, `created_at`, and the retire-in-place columns with their paired CHECK.
42-
43-**Plus:** a state column whose values are the project's existing cell states (derive them from the column CHECK they already carry: `grep -n -E "stated.*provisional.*pending.*not_applicable" scripts/migrations/*.sql | head`); a reviewed pair (`reviewed_at`, `reviewed_by`) set only by a review verb; one writer to propose a link (state `pending`) and one to review a batch (the owner's reviewed state), each refusing as `db.py` writers do (a blank warrant, an unknown code, a duplicate live row, a review that names no rows); and one view, `v_lens_crosswalk`, returning for an identity its needs and ICF codes, and for a need or an ICF code its identities, joined on the shared codes (a cross-stage view is the pointer, CLAUDE.md section 3).
44-
45-**Questions for the owner (the design cannot be finished without them):**
46-
47-1. **How many of the three must a row hold?** All three (a cell of the cube), or at least two (so identity–need, identity–ICF and need–ICF faces are all fillable, with the third left empty)? Recommended: at least two, because 11 identities have no ICF code and the maps cross at 2 codes.
48-2. **Who may mark a row stated?** Only the owner's review verb, or a session once a source attests it? Recommended: only a review the owner makes, per batch, as the owner confirmed on 2026-11-20.
49-3. **What becomes of `access_needs.absorbs` and the 61 + 43 rows of the two flat maps?** Kept and read as proposals (the design of 2026-11-15), or folded into the new table's rows? Recommended: kept as proposals now; `absorbs` retired in a later task once the table covers every need.
50-4. **Does a not-applicable row need a warrant?** Recommended: yes, the same cell as a stated row, because a quiet "does not apply" is the failure the cell states exist to prevent.

## 2. Delegation rules

### 2.1 Three delegation categories

| Code | Delegation | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| DG-NON | Non-delegable | The project owner alone. Other agents (Sonnet, Opus, contributors) propose; the project owner decides. |
| DG-REVIEW | Delegable with review | An agent decides; the project owner reviews before the decision is treated as canonical. The review may be batched (multiple decisions reviewed together) or per-decision. |
| DG-AUTO | Delegable / automatic | An agent decides; no review gate. Decision is logged; surfaces for review only if a downstream check flags inconsistency. |

### 2.2 Default delegation by category

| Decision category | Default delegation | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| D-DOCT | DG-NON | Doctrinal decisions reach into all downstream work; they cannot be delegated. |
| D-METH | DG-NON for new methodology; DG-REVIEW for application of existing methodology | The methodology itself is non-delegable; specific applications (e.g., classifying a new source's evidence tier) are delegable with review. |
| D-SCHEMA | DG-REVIEW | Schema choices that satisfy already-canonical methodology are delegable; novel schema patterns review-gated. |
| D-OP | DG-AUTO for routine operations; DG-REVIEW for first-of-kind | Branch-protection state, CI matrix updates, etc. are routine; the first commit-message convention or first session-file format is review-gated. |
| D-PRES | DG-AUTO within voice-style §§8.1–8.3 patterns; DG-REVIEW outside them | Pattern-conforming presentation decisions self-validate; novel patterns or pattern departures review-gated. |

### 2.3 Departure from default

A decision can depart from the default delegation. Departures are explicit: the decision record names the actual delegation and the reason. Common departure cases:

- A D-METH decision that has a doctrinal flow-through is recorded as DG-NON (delegation upgraded).
- A D-OP decision with material consequence (e.g., changing the PAT scope) is recorded as DG-REVIEW (delegation upgraded).
- A D-DOCT decision that merely operationalises a prior decision is recorded as DG-REVIEW (delegation downgraded).

Departures are visible in the decision record's `delegation` field and `delegation_rationale` field.

### 2.4 Non-delegable decisions explicitly

The following decision types are always DG-NON:

1. Mission, audience, and CRPD posture framing
2. Population taxonomy structure (codes, sub-codes, proxy decisions)
3. Evidence-tier definitions (1–6 + Co-1)
4. Inclusion/exclusion of jurisdictions
5. Inclusion/exclusion of major work-products (Volumes, Parts, Supplementary, Appendices)
6. Co-1 source corpus inclusion/exclusion
7. Licensing model (per A11 §4)
8. Trajectory positioning (per A11 §5)
9. Adversarial-use catalogue retirement (per A10 §5.4 — addition is DG-REVIEW)
10. Counsel-review queue resolution (per A11 §6)

---

## 3. Capture protocol

### 3.1 Every decision produces a written rationale

Bottom line: OD-73, OD-78 (clauses 3 and 4) and the proposed "T-102 without retiring SCI" ruling go back to the owner. The rest stand, most of them with corrections. Findings are ranked worst first.

---

**F1. CRITICAL. OD-73 decides what the owner meant and reverses the owner's explicit answer to T-145 §4 Q1. Ruling G item 2 itself bars that.**
- **What the owner was asked.** T-145 §4 Q1 (`grep -n -A3 "How many of the three" workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/tasks/T-145-identity-need-icf-triples.md`) asked: "All three … or at least two (so identity–need, identity–ICF and need–ICF faces are all fillable, with the third left empty)? Recommended: at least two." The owner refused that recommendation: "should be all three" (ledger 2026-11-20 fifth, line 8238 onward). Storing an identity–need face without an ICF code is exactly the capability the owner declined.
- **The adjudicator's answer is formalistic.** It says the answer "chose how many keys a row of that table holds" (adjudication line 97). Putting the same capability in a second table does not answer the owner's refusal.
- **The other basis supplies the owner's meaning.** The adjudicator reads "'Perhaps' qualifies only 'we select ICF codes'" (line 95). The 2026-11-22 ledger reading flagged that very word as an open question for the owner. Ruling G item 2 (line 14) says the delegate "cannot supply the owner's meaning".
- **Two binding records go unanswered.** The adjudication never names 2026-11-22 ACTION (2), "do not build a pairs table until the owner answers (OD-73)". Nor does it name the 2026-11-23 check's finding that R1–R4 "reverse part of the owner's own answer … not for a delegate to decide". Rule 0 requires a supersession to be named. It is not.
- **The grant does not carry it.** Under decision-protocol §2.2, D-SCHEMA is delegable only when it "satisf[ies] already-canonical methodology"; a novel pattern that contradicts an owner answer does not. Reading OD-73 into "approve and ratify" is the recorder's reading of 2026-11-25, which ACTION (5) marks unratified.
- **Verdict: REFERRED BACK.** Put it to the owner as one line: "You answered 'all three' to T-145 Q1, which declined storing identity–need pairs alone. Does 'map them to one another' (2026-11-22) now ask for a pairs table?"

**F2. HIGH. OD-78 clause 3 widens the 2026-11-21 (third) ACTION (2) and the 2026-11-23 interim. Its basis reads owner meaning into "etc" and into TRIPLE-64 and TRIPLE-65.**
- **It adds a kind of basis.** ACTION (2) of "Owner answer 2026-11-21 (third)" (line 8302 onward) admits three kinds of recorded basis: an owner statement, a recorded map row, or a WHO payload under T-128. "The session's own inference" is none of them. Clause 3 adds it while claiming it "narrows no owner word" (line 141).
- **It contradicts the interim.** The 2026-11-23 OD-78 interim says "no session cites a WHO payload for a relation between an identity and a code". Clauses 2 and 3 put the entity-page definition into the warrant of exactly such a relation.
- **The basis overreads the record:**
  - "'Etc' asks for more ties of this kind" (line 137). The ledger says "the generalisation is not decided here".
  - "The owner accepted TRIPLE-64 knowing …" (line 136). That is an [ASSUMPTION] reading in the ledger, stated as fact.
  - "The rejection concerned the pair, not the code." The ledger gives two reasons (a mislabelled warrant and the pair). TRIPLE-65's b164 was itself copied from `access_need_icf` A-TIME→b164. Re-derive: `select icf_code from identity_need_icf where triple_id=65`.
- **The "identity" half of clause 3 has no home.** No identity→b-code table exists except `identity_icf_map`, which OD-77 freezes. It also opens a route round TRIPLE-65's ACTION (2): a COM→b164 proposal keyed on the identity alone, with no need.
- **Verdict:** clauses 1–2 CONFIRMED as a rule for a code's existence and meaning (tabulation header checked: Foundation URI, Linearization URI, Code, BlockId, Title, ClassKind, DepthInKind, IsResidual, BrowserLink, isLeaf, CodingNote, Parent). Clause 2 is untested, because no entity page has been retrieved. Clauses 3–4 and the basis: REFERRED BACK.

**F3. HIGH. Part C says T-102 is held by "nothing now". Two holds are missed.**
- **OI-55(1), the carry-only research gate.** The task file says the gate is red by construction on R1, R9a and R9b, and the task must stop before `emit_data_migration` unless the ledger carries the owner's answer (`grep -n "red by construction for this batch" workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/tasks/T-102-mobility-split.md`; ISSUES-REGISTER ISS-005, OWNER-QUESTION). The ledger has no answer: `git grep -n "OI-55" -- references/project-standards.md` finds only an unrelated mention at line 6225.
- **OD-77's freeze.** T-102 step 3 writes seven new crossings, and step 4a moves SCI crossings, through `add-population-icf-link`. That verb INSERTs into `identity_icf_map` (`grep -n "INSERT INTO identity_icf_map" scripts/db.py` → line 10333). The adjudicator's own reading is "identity_icf_map stays frozen for new rows" (line 164).
- **Consequences.**
  - Next-step 1(d) ("An Opus session starts T-102") cannot land anything.
  - "Removes OI-77 from the head of the critical chain" (line 213) is false: OI-55(1) is at the head regardless.
  - The owner questions omit OI-55(1).

**F4. HIGH. The proposed OD "T-102 runs without retiring SCI; T-127/T-128 wait only for WHEEL" is population taxonomy in effect, and it defeats a stated precondition.**
- **It leaves two codes for one group.** It creates an interim lens with WHEEL and SCI both active, though the owner said they are one population (sixth set: "SCI is the same as WHEELCHAIR basically"). That is codes and proxy structure: decision-protocol §2.4 item 2, "always DG-NON".
- **It undoes T-127's stated reason.** T-127 §2 gives the reason for "SCI retired to it": "so a row is tagged `WHEEL` once and not … swept again" (`grep -n "swept again" workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/tasks/T-127-backfill-code-value-lenses.md`). Narrowing the precondition re-creates that double sweep for SCI figures. Count them: `select count(*) from extraction_lens_links where identity_code='SCI'`, which printed 3. The adjudicator did not address this.
- **It opens nothing anyway.** F3 holds T-102 regardless.
- **Verdict: REFERRED BACK.**

**F5. HIGH. Q3 asks the owner to retire rows the owner ruled count as coverage, without saying so.**
- **The reversal is hidden.** The rows that "only repeat a need's own environmental code" are 63 of the 64 live triples: `select count(*) from identity_need_icf t where retired_at is null and exists (select 1 from access_need_icf a where a.need_code=t.need_code and a.icf_code=t.icf_code)` prints 63; total live is 64. The owner ruled them coverage knowing they were copies: 2026-11-21 (sixth), "Yes, they count as identity's ICF coverage", whose ACTION (1) is "do not file or build a change that excludes it". The question put to the owner then had called them "copied". The adjudicator's rule-5 argument weighs the paperwork against a live ruling, which rule 0 forbids. Q3 does not tell the owner it reverses their own answer.
- **The bundle is too wide.** Q3 also folds three things into one yes/no: GAP-379's open A-TRIGGER question (left open by 2026-11-21 second, ACTION (2)), 27 pair acceptances and 2 rejections, and that retirement.
- **Q4's "not now" holds. Correction:** unbundle Q3, and name the 2026-11-21 (sixth) answer it would reverse.

**F6. MEDIUM. Class B leans on the owner's umbrella answer beyond its words, and calls the recommendation a delegated resolution (Ruling G item 1).**
- **The umbrella answer reaches only NDV.** "To umbrella and to specific, yes" answered umbrella-versus-member identities (NDV over AUT and ADHD). BRAIN, COM, MH and EPI rows are keyed on a whole identity for one listed condition (post-concussion, MCAS, PTSD, photosensitivity), which is not an umbrella/member relation. EPI is not an umbrella at all.
- **It would answer an open owner question.** "Accepting COM–A-TRIGGER and EPI–A-TRIGGER answers GAP-379's open sub-question" decides what a group needs. That stays the owner's.
- **It should not be a resolution.** Line 179: "this per-pair recommendation, recorded as a delegated resolution". A per-pair statement that a group has a need is DG-NON by Ruling G item 1. It may be a recommendation in an owner question, never an OD status line.
- **The split itself is right.** I re-derived it from live warrants: 29 pairs; 14 + 3 = 17 class A; 7 + 3 = 10 class B; 2 class C (BRAIN–A-NOSPEECH, COM–A-LOWLOAD).

**F7. MEDIUM. The "mapping" lean is contrary to the record, and the timestamp trace read only assistant prose.**
- **What the trace missed.** Two seconds before the owner typed (04:04:08), the tool result at 04:04:06.335 (transcript line 152) printed the identity table with a column "ICF codes (`identity_icf_map`, live rows)". The T-128 file describing `identity_icf_map` was read at 04:02:58 (line 97). Whether the owner saw either cannot be verified.
- **The owner's own complaint points the other way.** The first message objects to "entire groups like b750 to b789". Range codes held by each table:
  - `identity_icf_map`: 11
  - `identity_need_icf`: 0
  - `access_need_icf`: 0
  - Command: `select count(*) from <t> x join base_icf b using(icf_code) where b.is_range=1` (plus `retired_at is null` where the column exists).
- **So:** "weight of the record leans towards the PR 245 rows" (line 160) is unsupported, and Q2 is framed so that "yes" means PR 245.
- **Verdict on the hold ruling: CONFIRMED WITH CORRECTIONS.** Strike the lean, and put Q2 neutrally with both candidates and the range evidence.

**F8. MEDIUM. The pairs-table design is wrong in three places, though its partial-index claim holds.**
- **The claim holds:** SQLite 3.53.1 refuses a partial unique index as an FK parent ("foreign key mismatch").
- **The alternative design was missed.** "R2's FK and the antagonist's partial index cannot both stand" ignores a surrogate key. `ALTER TABLE identity_need_icf ADD COLUMN pair_id INTEGER REFERENCES identity_need(pair_id)` works beside the partial index, tested on a scratch copy. The ruling instead leaves no schema link: a triple with no pair INSERTs cleanly (tested), so the R4 verb is the only guard.
- **"Copied unchanged" does not work.** Migration 166's no-edit trigger does not list the new `inferred` column. On the scratch copy, `inferred` flipped 0→1→0 freely after the trigger was copied. The review verb's binding is to the token `TRIPLE-<id>` (`grep -n "TRIPLE-<id>" scripts/db.py` → line 2407), so a pairs review needs its own token. The guards must be extended, not copied.
- These defects stand whether or not OD-73 survives F1.

**F9. MEDIUM. The owner is misquoted in Q1.**
- **Where:** Q1 (line 219) says "as you said on 2026-11-12 ('only SCI is the same as WHEEL')". Lines 191 and 195 quote the same phrase.
- **What the phrase really is:** the recorder's ledger heading at line 6129. The transcript shows the assistant writing it in a heredoc at 2026-11-12T21:14:58 (transcripts/harness_4a95df3b/main.jsonl).
- **The owner's typed words were:** "except SCI is the same as WHEELCHAIR basically and LMB is the same as PROSTHETIC" (line 6115).

**F10. MEDIUM. The proposed "import every 3-digit category" OD overstates its warrant.**
- "S1's words state it" is a delegate's reading of "all the codes bundled under those umbrellas", which could equally mean the codes the project holds.
- The 3-digit grain is the delegate's choice. Read literally, "all" would include 4-digit codes.
- It supersedes OD-74's checked correction ("the rest only if the owner says so"). That is allowed for a method decision on WHO's vocabulary, but it must be named as a delegated reading.
- Re-derived size: 373 three-digit categories in the payload (regex `[bdes]\d{3}` over the Code column).
- **Verdict: CONFIRMED WITH CORRECTIONS.** Strike "S1's words state it"; record the grain as the delegate's choice.

**F11. LOW. Ruling G cites the wrong clause.** It rests on decision-protocol §2.3 ("a departure must be explicit"). §2.4 says those items are "always DG-NON", which is stronger. The conclusion stands. Ruling G is also not itself given a status or check line, though the "Standing" paragraph covers it.

**F12. LOW. A false claim about the generator.** Part C says the generator "writes REMEDIATION-PLAN.md despite its docstring". The docstring (line 2 of build_batches.py) says "Reads only; writes REMEDIATION-PLAN.md." It says the same thing.

---

**What held.**
- **Constraints check (5).** No "Owner" heading appears. No guard is relaxed. Every ruling reads "check pending". The adjudicator's transcript (`~/.claude/projects/.../subagents/agent-a20a18eb39ae291f1.jsonl`) shows one Write, to adjudication.md, and no tree-writing Bash call. `data/guidebook.db`, `workplan/` and `references/` are unchanged. `scripts/db.py`, `dbcore.py` and `test_icf_hierarchy.py` have mtimes after adjudication.md's (21:16–21:17 against 21:15:09), which fits the coordinator's statement that those edits are its own.

- OD-73: REFERRED BACK (F1, F8)

- **The other basis supplies the owner's meaning.** The adjudicator reads "'Perhaps' qualifies only 'we select ICF codes'" (line 95). The 2026-11-22 ledger reading flagged that very word as an open question for the owner. Ruling G item 2 (line 14) says the delegate "cannot supply the owner's meaning".

Nor does it name the 2026-11-23 check's finding that R1–R4 "reverse part of the owner's own answer … not for a delegate to decide". Rule 0 requires a supersession to be named. It is not.
- **The grant does not carry it.** Under decision-protocol §2.2, D-SCHEMA is delegable only when it "satisf[ies] already-canonical methodology"; a novel pattern that contradicts an owner answer does not. Reading OD-73 into "approve and ratify" is the recorder's reading of 2026-11-25, which ACTION (5) marks unratified.

**F2. HIGH. OD-78 clause 3 widens the 2026-11-21 (third) ACTION (2) and the 2026-11-23 interim. Its basis reads owner meaning into "etc" and into TRIPLE-64 and TRIPLE-65.**

"The session's own inference" is none of them. Clause 3 adds it while claiming it "narrows no owner word" (line 141).

def _identity_carriers(conn, code):
    """Every live row that still carries identity `code`: (table.column, n). DERIVED from the foreign keys into
    base_taxonomy_identity (never listed). `evidence_population_match.target_population` (free text, no foreign key) is NOT a
    carrier: it is a record, counted apart by `_identity_records`. A row is live unless its table carries a retirement mark
    and it is set; a code's own successor pointers and a retired child's parent_code are not carriers."""
    out = []
    tables = [r[0] for r in conn.execute("SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name NOT LIKE 'sqlite_%'")]
    # RECORDS are not carriers: a logged search and a graded population match say what happened and were true when
    # written, and no verb re-tags either, so counting them would make a retirement impossible (the 2026-11-15
    # critic showed SCI could not be retired). They are counted apart by `_identity_records`.
    pairs = [(t, f[3]) for t in tables for f in conn.execute(f'PRAGMA foreign_key_list("{t}")')
             if f[2] == "base_taxonomy_identity" and t not in _IDENTITY_RECORD_COLS]
    for t, col in pairs:
        cols = set(dbcore.columns(conn, t))
        if col not in cols:
            continue
        where = f'"{col}" = ?'
        if "retired_at" in cols:
            where += " AND retired_at IS NULL"
        if "resolved_at" in cols:                      # a resolved gate is history
            where += " AND resolved_at IS NULL"
        if t == "gaps":                                # a closed gap is history
            where += " AND status LIKE 'OPEN%'"
        if t == "base_taxonomy_identity" and col == "parent_code":
            where += " AND status = 'active'"
        if t == "base_taxonomy_identity" and col == "superseded_by_identity":
            where += " AND status = 'deprecated'"      # a code another deprecated code names as its successor
        n = conn.execute(f'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "{t}" WHERE {where}', (code,)).fetchone()[0]
        if n:
            out.append((f"{t}.{col}", n))
    return out

Never claim a batch is done from your own reading of it. Run the gate the
SessionStart contract names:

```
python3 scripts/audit/research_batch_dod.py --session "$(cat scratchpad/CURRENT)"
python3 scripts/audit/adversarial_pass_audit.py --session "$(cat scratchpad/CURRENT)"
python3 scripts/audit/search_log_completeness.py --session "$(cat scratchpad/CURRENT)"
python3 scripts/audit/refusal_register.py classes --session "$(cat scratchpad/CURRENT)"
```

The second line is RC4 (advisory): it FAILs if this session wrote to any of the 2026-08-19
RULE's research tables and no closed adversarial pass names it. That FAIL is not a reason to
close pass 1; LED-192 holds it open (`/adversarial` step 3). Run it on `CURRENT`, not via
`run_checks.py --all --battery research` — that battery's other session-scoped checks
(`research_dod_session`, `citation_mining_session`) are still pointed at `LATEST-RESEARCH`,
which names the PREVIOUS session for the whole life of this one. (`author_fidelity` reads
every source against every session's retrievals, so it does see this batch.)

The third line is I5, also on `CURRENT`: it reads the WebSearch/WebFetch ledger the
harness hook wrote and FAILs a WebSearch query that no `search_executions.query_text` of
this session contains — a search you ran and did not log (R8). Log it with
`db.py log-search --backfill 1`: the row is a reconstruction, not a log made as the search
ran, and the `--prior-expectation` it still requires is written after the results, so it
is post hoc and must say so. Its REPORTED lines (unpersisted WebFetch URLs, bare curl/wget
hosts, and web rows logged with no web line on the ledger — a hook that may not have
fired) belong in the session record; they do not fail, and a NOTHING-IN-SCOPE verdict does
DOWN only, and raising a count there forgives fresh violations invisibly.

When it passes, confirm the corpus posture has not regressed:

```
python3 scripts/audit/research_batch_dod.py --all
```

Then commit the scratchpad and the agent transcripts (`scripts/preserve_transcripts.py`)
— a read-only subagent writes nothing at all, so its entire workings live in
ephemeral container storage until they are copied out.
